values.note: recreation.gov 2026 and 2027: $26 per site in every season. The Forest Service page (updated February 2026) posts $28 per night, $11 for a third vehicle and $11 day use. Two vehicles or one RV included.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234737/rates (2026 and 2027 Peak and First-come seasons: STANDARD NONELECTRIC 26) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground ('Single Site: $28 per night', 'Additional Vehicle Fee: $11 for third vehicle'; last updated February 3, 2026), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Forest Service: 'open late May to late December' (its Seasons of Use line says early May). Full service Memorial Day to Labor Day weekend; water, trash or a host may be missing in the fall extended season. 2026 dates are recreation.gov's fee seasons (reservable May 22 - Sept 6, first-come Sept 7 - Dec 31).

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground ('The campground is open late May to late December. Full service is available from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day weekend.'; 'Seasons of Use: Early May to late December') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234737/rates (2026 seasons 05-22 to 12-31), read 2026-10-26

hookups.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground ('There is no dump station or hook-up available') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234737 (notice 'no water hookups') + campsite catalog for 234737 (all NONELECTRIC), read 2026-10-26

values.note: 12 RV/tent sites (max vehicle lengths 24-50 ft, two pull-throughs) and one tent-only site; 7 reservable, 6 first-come.

sites.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 234737 (site types, reservable flag, Max Vehicle Length, Driveway Entry) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234737 ('Burning Bear Campground has 13 sites to accommodate RV, trailer and tent camping'), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Water is from a hand pump; recreation.gov: 'a/o 8/3/2026 the hand pump is down and will not be available for the remainder of this season (2026)', so bring all water.

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground ('Restrooms: Vault toilets'; 'Potable water is available at a hand pump'; 'There is no dump station') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234737 (notice quoted), read 2026-10-26

values.note: Reserve at least four days ahead on recreation.gov or 877-444-6777 for the 2026 season May 22 - Sept 6; first-come from Sept 7 to the end of December, and 6 sites are always first-come. Reserved weekends need Friday and Saturday nights, holiday weekends three; 'Walk-ups are exempt from the nightly minimum.' 14 consecutive nights at most.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground ('Call 877-444-6777 or visit recreation.gov at least four days in advance. A Friday and Saturday night minimum stay is required on weekends. A three-night minimum stay is required on holiday weekends. Walk-ups are exempt from the nightly minimum.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234737 (facility_rules maxConsecutiveStay 14, reservationCutOff 4; notice 'Facility has first-come, first-serve sites') + /rates (2026 Peak 05-22 to 09-06, First-come 09-07 to 12-31), read 2026-10-26

values.note: 50% off the site the pass holder occupies (concessionaire-run sites).

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground ('The Interagency Senior Pass and the Interagency Access Pass qualify for a 50% discount at concessionaire-run campsites'), read 2026-10-26

note: On the Guanella Pass Scenic Byway 5 miles north of Grant (South Platte RD, Pike-San Isabel NF) at 9,800 ft, below the Mount Evans Wilderness; Burning Bear Trail across the road. Dirt aprons, and recreation.gov warns of a rough campground road (potholes, washboard). The road is plowed this far from Grant but drifts heavily. --Claude
summary: Confirmed 13 sites to 50 ft, no hookups, reservable on recreation.gov. Fee: recreation.gov $26 (2026-27) recorded; the FS page says $28. Added season late May - Dec 31 (FS 'late May to late December'), reservable season 05-22 to 09-06, some sites FCFS, 4-day cutoff, FS-stated 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimums for reservations, 14-night limit, vault toilets, hand-pump water (down for the rest of 2026), no dump, senior/access 50%. No current alert on Guanella Pass Road (CR 62).
flags: Fee conflict: recreation.gov's 2026 and 2027 rate table says $26, the Forest Service page (updated February 2026) says $28 (and $11 per extra vehicle). Recorded $26.

Access: recreation.gov notices 'Expect rough road conditions and erosion: potholes and wash-boarding' and 'the campground road may be rough'; no 4WD or high-clearance wording anywhere, and the access is 5 miles up the Guanella Pass Scenic and Historic Byway (Park County 62) from Grant. Kept as a note caveat, not a criteria problem.

Entry phone is empty. The Forest Service page gives South Platte Ranger District 303-275-5610; recreation.gov also gives (303) 647-2366 'for facility specific information'. Concession-run per the FS pass wording; no concessionaire named.
Agency page for the website if wanted: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/psicc/recreation/burning-bear-campground (website is the recreation.gov listing).
